title: Zero service requests in three trials
scenario_markdown: Over 3 independent customer visits, each customer has a 20% probability ($p=0.20$) of requesting technical service. Find the probability that none of the three customers request service.
assumptions: Two outcomes per visit: service or no service

approval.notes: Reviewed derivation for n=3, p=0.2, k=0 yielding P(X=0) = (0.8)^3 = 0.512. 3 stages with 1-to-1 concept evidence mapping.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which event formulation represents 'none of the three customers request service'?

options.hint_markdown: None means zero successes, not one.

stages.explanation_markdown: 'None' corresponds to zero service requests, so the event is $X = 0$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate $P(X = 0)$. Enter decimal, percent, or fraction.
What does $P(X = 0) = 0.512$ tell us about the frequency of zero-request visits?

options.text_markdown: In slightly more than half of all three-visit sets (51.2%), no customer requests service.
Zero requests is an extremely rare outlier event.
options.hint_markdown: A probability of 0.512 is greater than 50%.

options.text_markdown: Zero requests is guaranteed to occur on every visit.
options.hint_markdown: 0.512 is not 1.0; requests can and do occur.

stages.explanation_markdown: $0.512$ translates to $51.2\%$, meaning a majority of three-visit sets will see zero requests.
